adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] Removed duplicate-group-key guard means duplicate keys from a stateful handler's get_group_key_values are now silently deduplicated by dict overwrite instead of logging 'Duplicate detector state group keys found', losing the investigation signal

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `DetectorHandler.evaluate`/`StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` instead of a `list`, and `StatefulDetectorHandler.get_group_key_values` is typed/used as a `dict[str, int]`. With these dict-based interfaces, duplicate group keys are not representable at the API boundary (a dict cannot contain duplicate keys), so the removed duplicate-key logging guard in `process_detectors` no longer applies to `get_group_key_values` outputs. The old duplicate-key test (`group_keys=["dupe","dupe"]`) is deleted and replaced with dict-based `group_vals`, reflecting the intentional API shift rather than a newly introduced silent dedupe of handler output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] PriorityLevel(new_status) assumes DetectorPriorityLevel and PriorityLevel share identical member values; divergence would raise ValueError at evaluation time — map explicitly or have the state layer use PriorityLevel directly

adjudication.rationale: In `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate_group_key_value`, the new code calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, PriorityLevel(new_status))` where `new_status` is a `DetectorPriorityLevel` (from `sentry.workflow_engine.types`). This implicitly converts between two different enum types (`DetectorPriorityLevel` -> `PriorityLevel`) and will only work if their underlying values align; otherwise `PriorityLevel(...)` can raise `ValueError`. The diff doesn’t show the enum definitions, so a concrete mismatch isn’t verifiable here, but the concern is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] No test covers the resolved (new_status == OK) path through process_detectors/produce_occurrence_to_kafka with status_change populated; only occurrence-producing paths are asserted against the producer

adjudication.rationale: In the updated tests, `TestProcessDetectors.test_state_results` and `test_state_results_multi_group` patch `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` and only assert calls where `status_change=None` and an `occurrence` is provided. The resolved/OK path is exercised in `TestEvaluate.test_above_below_threshold` via `handler.evaluate(...)` returning a `DetectorEvaluationResult` whose `result` is a `StatusChangeMessage`, but that test does not run through `process_detectors` nor assert any `produce_occurrence_to_kafka` call with `status_change` populated. So the producer path for `new_status == OK` through `process_detectors` is not covered by an assertion in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] StatusChangeMessage.__eq__ patcher is entered in setUp and exited in tearDown without try/finally; if setUp raises after __enter__, the patch leaks to other tests — use addCleanup instead

adjudication.rationale: In `BaseDetectorHandlerTest.setUp`, the patcher is manually entered via `self.sm_comp_patcher.__enter__()` and only exited in `tearDown` (`__exit__`). If an exception occurs later in `setUp` (after `__enter__`), `tearDown` will not run and the `StatusChangeMessage.__eq__` patch can leak into other tests. Using `addCleanup(self.sm_comp_patcher.__exit__, ...)` or `self.addCleanup(patcher.stop)` would make cleanup robust.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] DetectorHandler.evaluate return type changed from list[DetectorEvaluationResult] to dict, breaking external/custom handler subclasses with no deprecation or compatibility shim

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes the abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract from returning `list[DetectorEvaluationResult]` to returning `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (see `DetectorHandler.evaluate` signature and `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate`). Call sites (`process_detectors`) were updated to iterate `detector_results.values()`, and tests/subclasses in-tree were adjusted accordingly. While this isn’t a correctness bug within the updated code, it is an API-breaking change for any out-of-tree/custom `DetectorHandler` subclasses that still implement/return a list, and the diff shows no compatibility shim or deprecation path.
